title: Transformer pipeline predicts MSI from colorectal cancer histology across 16 cohorts
summary: A transformer encoder combined with transformer patch aggregation predicted biomarkers from H&E slides, using over 13,000 patients from 16 colorectal cancer cohorts. For microsatellite instability on resection specimens it reached sensitivity 0.99 with negative predictive value above 0.99, and resection-only training reached clinical-grade performance on endoscopic biopsies. The study is retrospective.
ai_technology: Pre-trained transformer encoder with a transformer network for patch aggregation on pathology slides
organization: Helmholtz Munich; Else Kröner Fresenius Center for Digital Health; Technical University of Munich

evidence.tested: Biomarker prediction was evaluated on large multicenter cohorts, including biopsy tissue.
evidence.unknown: Prospective clinical use is not tested. Abstract-based; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: The transformer pipeline predicted MSI and other biomarkers directly from routine H&E slides.
